before.label: before-respawn
gameplay_oracle_reasons: the PlayerController possesses no pawn (AController::Pawn is null): the player has not spawned yet

provenance.why: the capture harness did not record it -- slow_pass built its snapshot from Resolver directly instead of through resolve_live(), where that field was set. Fixed in the harness; these two files predate the fix.
provenance.how_established: measured directly from the still-running process: pid 8676 started 2026-08-30T09:29:24Z and is still alive. Process continuity across the capture is independently supported: the 50 ms poll ran without interruption against pid 8676 from t=0 to t=495.146, and the PlayerController pointer 0x20092403740 was identical at both ends -- a restart would have given a fresh heap and a different pointer.
provenance.limit: this is a post-hoc stamp, not a capture-time reading. Future runs record it at capture time.
provenance.independently_established_by_verifier: An independent verifier supplied the decisive argument, stronger than the circumstantial one first written here: pid 8676 is alive with start_time 2026-08-30T09:29:24Z. A live process has held its pid continuously since its own start time, so NO other process can have held pid 8676 between 09:29:24Z and now. Both snapshots resolved pid 8676 inside that window (13:13:24Z and 13:21:51Z), so they read THIS process. That holds without the stamp. Independently, snap-launch4-gameplay.json carries the same start time with NO provenance block -- a genuine capture-time reading through resolve_live().

same_process.evidence_grade: MIXED: 2 of 3 snapshots carry a post-hoc stamp rather than a capture-time reading. The claim rests on whatever independent argument those stamps record, not on the field itself.
same_process.why_it_matters: object identity is only comparable inside one process: a new process has a new heap, and identical paths there are different objects. If this were false, every verdict below would be void.

possession.note: both routes are read independently and the resolver refuses unless they agree, so a resolved pawn anchor IS the agreement

transition_observability.limit: Pawn and AcknowledgedPawn became non-null AND equal within a single 50 ms sample, so any intermediate state where Pawn was set but AcknowledgedPawn was not lasted less than one sampling interval. That is a limit of this instrument, not evidence that no such state existed.

death_evidence.death_screen_live_is_not_evidence: BP_DeathScreen_C is live in the healthy post-respawn state on this build too, so its presence does not distinguish death from life and is recorded, not relied on

respawn_evidence.why_both_are_required: an agreement alone would also be produced by arming the watch during ordinary gameplay; only the pair no-pawn -> possessed-pawn is a respawn
